blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Northeast Maple Ridge

items.t: Form B diligence (any future strata townhouse): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with rules, current budget and the most recent depreciation report attached.

: a Northeast acreage purchase has NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees — municipal rules (Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019), ALR rules where they apply, and any registered covenants on title govern. That is the frame for the stock that actually exists in this sub-area.

Maple Ridge zoning: Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 governs; its schedule minimum lot areas include A-1 2.0 ha, A-2 4.0 ha, A-3 8.0 ha, A-4 1.8 ha, A-5 8.0 ha, RS-2 0.4 ha, RS-3 0.8 ha or 2.0 ha (refer to zone text), RS-1d 2,000 m² and RS-1c 1,200 m².

OCP citation — CONTESTED, flagged, never resolved: What is settled for this sub-area: the North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan (OCP amendments covering both sides of 256 Street north of 128 Avenue, about 500 acres) establishes future designations and does not itself approve construction, and the OCP's Thornhill Urban Reserve designation identifies lands for long-term future urban services and housing.

Suites / SSMUH as Maple Ridge states them: one secondary suite per lot is permitted in listed zones including A-1, A-2 and A-3, contained within the single detached building, to a maximum of 40% of gross floor area, and not in the Floodplain Area; on ALR parcels the ALR Use Regulation also governs — one secondary suite in the principal residence (s. 31), an additional residence only if the s. 32 conditions are met. A suite is a fee-simple second unit, never a townhouse.

GST and rebates (for a new-build purchase elsewhere in the city): 5% GST on new construction only; the FTHB GST rebate — Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026 per CRA News No. 122 — rebates 100% of GST to $1M (maximum $50,000), phasing to $1.5M, agreements March 20, 2025–2031; the New Housing Rebate is 36% / maximum $6,300 / $350K–$450K.

PTT + exemptions, compression flagged: 1% on the first $200,000 / 2% to $2M / 3% above, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3M — a page's "Over $3M — 5%" row compresses that 3% + 2%. First-time buyer exemption: no tax on the first $500,000 up to $835,000, partial to $860,000; Newly Built Home Exemption full to $1,100,000, phasing out at $1,150,000. HBP $60,000; FHSA $40,000 lifetime / $8,000 per year; CMHC premiums 0.6%–4.5%.

blocks.text: Good to know about Northeast Maple Ridge

items.t: "Northeast" is a board name the City does not use: The City of Maple Ridge's neighbourhoods page lists its named neighbourhoods and Northeast is not among them; the ground is administered as Ruskin, Thornhill, Webster's Corners, Whonnock and Yennadon.

The 500-acre industrial plan sits inside a residential acreage pitch: The North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan covers both sides of 256 Street north of 128 Avenue (about 500 acres), where existing uses already include gravel extraction, institutional operations and civic services — a buyer pricing a quiet forested acreage on 256 Street north of 128 Avenue is pricing beside a designated future industrial area, and the plan's own access case (Abernethy Way, Lougheed Highway, the Golden Ears Bridge, the South Fraser Perimeter Road) is the reason. The plan approves no construction itself; the designation is the fact.

The sample catchment address is the school's own address: The locator result recorded for Northeast used 25554 Dewdney Trunk Road — Webster's Corners Elementary's own address — and returned Webster's Corners Elementary and Garibaldi Secondary. It settles that one address only; SD42 also runs Samuel Robertson Technical Secondary inside this sub-area, so a listing that names a secondary school for any other Northeast address without a locator run for that address is ahead of the evidence.
